old_problem: The missing specification defines whether an I2C transaction is benign observation or fan-control hazard. DeepSeek cannot identify FAN_BD, its mux branch or expected resources, may contend with active thermal control, and claims no risk without collecting RPM, PWM, tach fault or temperature evidence.
disposition_reason: Retain Pending and BLOCKED. A parameterized test still needs an approved physical fan-resource map and register-level read allowlist; neither can be inferred from host bus enumeration. Wrong access can alter PWM/watchdog/control behavior or obscure tach data. Exact expected values, thermal aborts and independent cooling recovery are core safety and PASS semantics.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1803, same-row DeepSeek/test-json, GPT V2, historical record, pending/blocked analyses and ED-01 through ED-30 were read. The next formal locked-queue identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1804 / Wistron-HW-00006-V003 / 1b1a5a481c05cebb.
FAN_BD I2C defaults to BMC/platform-management scope and requires the owning controller/mux, physical fan mapping and expected response.
Finding an address cannot prove correct fan identity, tach/PWM resource mapping, valid telemetry or unchanged cooling control.
ED-03 forbids guessed OEM paths/registers and ED-15 forbids PASS without approved RPM, PWM, temperature and fault thresholds.
Cooling safety requires independent monitoring/recovery and immediate stop without automatic retry on any fan or thermal anomaly.
No SSH, I2C, fan-control, scan, write, reset, retry or DUT action was performed.
